source_quote: The College of Engineering at Rafik Hariri University (RHU) was established in 1999.
answer: The College of Engineering was established in 1999 and offers six undergraduate programs (Biomedical, Civil, Computer and Communications, Electrical, Mechanical, Mechatronics), accredited by the Lebanese Ministry of Higher Education, with master's programs in all six and more than 400 students enrolled.

source_quote: master’s degree option is also available. More than 400 students are currently enrolled
answer: Master's programs are available in all six engineering programs; employed students who can only attend in the afternoons have a non-thesis master's option.

source_quote: The College of Engineering aspires to be a center of excellence in engineering education
answer: CE vision: a center of excellence in engineering education and an incubator for innovation serving Lebanon, the region and the world. Mission: quality professional education enabling students to innovate practical solutions to society's problems.

source_quote: Accreditation Commission (EAC) of ABET, 415 North Charles Street, Baltimore, MD
answer: The Bachelor of Engineering programs in Biomedical, Civil, Computer and Communications, Electrical, Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission (EAC) of ABET.

source_quote: The College of Engineering offers six undergraduate programs leading to a Bachelor of
answer: The College of Engineering offers BS and BE degrees in Civil, Electrical, Computer and Communications, Biomedical, Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering, and an MS in each of these six fields.
Engineering course prefixes: CIVE Civil, BIOM Biomedical, CCEE Computer and Communications, ELEC Electrical and Electronics, MECH Mechanical, MECA Mechatronics Engineering.

Engineering applicants who did not submit SAT scores may have to take math and physics placement exams depending on their Lebanese Baccalaureate scores; failing requires passing a related remedial course.

source_quote: A student must choose the degree that s/he wishes to
answer: Each engineering program offers a BS or a BE. The text gives the BS as 116 credits and the BE as 152 credits; students must choose their degree before completing 60 credits. The first three years are common to both (except the BS project), and the BS is earned after the first three years of the study plan.
review_note: p.269 text says the BS has 116 credits, but the BS credit table (p.270) and p.28 give 118.

answer: Engineering students graduate after completing all degree requirements with a cumulative GPA, major GPA and Summative Learning Project grade of 70 or above, and a passing grade on the Co-op work experience.

source_quote: BE degree in the same major may reapply for admission to the BE program. However,
answer: RHU BS engineering graduates who want the BE in the same major may reapply for admission to the BE program and must take a 3-credit technical elective to replace the BS project.

BE (152 credits) distribution: CIVE, BIOM, MECH, MECA - General Education 20 mandatory + 10 elective, College 27, Program 80 mandatory + 15 elective; CCEE - GE 17 + 13, College 27, Program 77 + 18; ELEC - GE 20 + 10, College 24 + 3 elective, Program 80 + 15. Totals: GE 30, College 27, Program 95.

BS (118 credits) distribution: CIVE, BIOM, MECH, MECA - GE 20 + 7, College 24, Program 67; CCE - GE 17 + 10, College 14, Program 67; ELEC - GE 20 + 7, College 21 + 3, Program 67. Totals: GE 27, College 23, Program 67.
review_note: Row totals for CCE (17+10+14+67=108) do not equal 118; table values may be misprinted.

source_quote: Every BE (BS)- bound student is required to take 30 (27) credits of general education
answer: Engineering gen-ed: 30 credits (BE) or 27 (BS). Communication 9 (ENGL 210, ENGL 217, ARAB 212, 1-credit Community and Sustainability elective); Humanities/Fine Arts 3; Social Sciences/Culture 6; Natural Sciences and Technology 6 (CCEE 214 or COSC 214 plus CHEM 211 for CIVE/MECH/MECA, PHYS 312 for ELEC/BIOM, a science elective for CCEE); Quantitative Reasoning 6 (MATH 351 and ENGR 300).

source_quote: Understanding of the basic principles of programming and computer systems;
answer: CCEE 214 Introduction to Programming + Lab, 3(2,1): programming principles applied to engineering problems - control structures, functions, arrays, pointers and structures - with lab experiments; equivalent to COSC 214.

answer: All incoming engineering students sit for math and physics placement exams and may need one or two remedial courses: MATH 190, MATH 191, PHYS 190 (MECH/MECA/CIVE) or PHYS 191 (ELEC/CCE/BIOM). Remedial courses do not count toward the degree.

source_quote: All Engineering students (BS and BE) are required to take 24 credit hours of college-
answer: All engineering students take 24 credits of college-required courses (BE adds ENGR 510 Engineering Project Management): mathematics (MATH 210 for CCE only, MATH 215, 216, 311, 314, 421 for all, MATH 317 for MECH/MECA), sciences (BIOL 210 for BIOM, GEOL 221 for CIVE, PHYS 210 for MECH/MECA/CIVE, PHYS 211 for ELEC/CCE/BIOM, science elective for ELEC), and ELEC 210 Electric Circuits.
The engineering college requirements list MATH 216 Calculus IV as 2 credits.
